name: Rice (Paddy)
soilType: Clayey loam, alluvial soil with good water retention
growthTips: Maintain 2-5 cm standing water during tillering to panicle initiation.
Apply neem-coated urea in split doses (basal, tillering, panicle initiation).
Use certified seeds treated with Carbendazim (2g/kg seed).

commonDiseases.name: Rice Blast
symptoms: Spindle-shaped spots with grey-white center and brown margin on leaves
Dark brown lesions at node and neck of panicle
causes: Frequent cloudy days with intermittent rains
organicTreatment: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 2.5 kg/ha in 500L water
Apply 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) spray
Avoid stagnant flood water during high humidity
chemicalTreatment: Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L water at first sign of leaf spots
prevention: Use resistant varieties like Swarna, IR-64, or MTU-1010
Treat seeds with Tricyclazole before nursery sowing

commonDiseases.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB)
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions turning yellow-white along leaf margins
Milky bacterial ooze visible in early morning droplets
organicTreatment: Spray fresh cow dung filtrate (20g/L) + Hing (Asafoetida) spray
Drain excess stagnant water for 3 days to aerate roots
chemicalTreatment: Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L water combined with Copper Oxychloride @ 2 g/L water
prevention: Avoid clipping seedlings tip at transplanting
Adopt alternate wetting and drying (AWD) irrigation

name: Tomato
soilType: Well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter (pH 6.0 - 7.0)
growthTips: Provide sturdy bamboo staking at 30 days after transplanting.
Mulch with straw or black plastic to prevent soil-borne splash infections.
Drip irrigation at root level is superior to overhead sprinkler watering.

commonDiseases.name: Early Blight
symptoms: Concentric dark brown rings on older lower leaves (target board pattern)
Yellowing halo surrounding the brown rings
Stem lesions at soil line (collar rot)
causes: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) accompanied by heavy dew or rains
organicTreatment: Spray 10% Cow urine + 5% Neem leaf extract spray every 7 days
Prune and destroy infected lower leaves immediately
prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops for 3 years
Stake plants upright to keep leaves away from soil

commonDiseases.name: Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV)
symptoms: Severe upward and downward curling and puckering of leaves
Stunted bushy plant growth with short internodes
Flower shedding and failure to set fruits
causes: Whitefly insect population explosion in dry, warm weather
organicTreatment: Install yellow sticky traps @ 20-25 traps/acre to trap whiteflies
Spray 5% Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) or 10,000 ppm Azadirachtin @ 2 mL/L
Intercrop with barrier crops like maize or sorghum on field borders
prevention: Protect seedlings in nursery with 40-mesh insect-proof nylon nets
Uproot and bury severely infected viral plants

name: Cotton
soilType: Deep black cotton soil (Regur), alluvial well-drained loam
growthTips: Do not apply excess nitrogen after flowering to avoid boll rot and excessive vegetative growth.
Install pheromone traps @ 5 per acre to monitor Pink Bollworm moths.
Nipping/topping of terminal shoots at 90 days boosts boll development.

commonDiseases.name: Pink Bollworm & American Bollworm
symptoms: Rosetted flowers with petals twisted together
Bored holes on bolls with excreta at the entrance
Stained fiber and premature boll opening (locule rot)
causes: Warm dry weather and lack of timely trap crop management
organicTreatment: Install 8 Pheromone traps/acre with Gossyplure lures
Release Trichogramma bactrae egg parasitoids @ 60,000/acre at weekly intervals
Spray Beauveria bassiana @ 5g/L water in evening hours
prevention: Strictly terminate crop before January to break pest lifecycle
Plant non-Bt refuge cotton / castor border rows
